ui_state.question: A $100M mortgage pool (80% Senior, 15% Mezzanine, 5% Equity) suffers a $14M collateral default loss. How much loss does the Mezzanine tranche absorb?
ui_state.explanation: Correct! Total Loss = $14M. Equity absorbs the first $5M (100% loss). Residual Loss = $14M - $5M = $9M. Mezzanine absorbs $9M out of its $15M principal ($9M / $15M = 60.0%). Senior Tranche takes $0 loss.

beats.en_narration: Here is your executive review of the 8 Iron Laws governing securitization, ABS CDOs, and the post-crisis financial architecture.

ui_state.threadTitle: The 8 Iron Laws of Securitization & Subprime Meltdown
ui_state.threadSubtitle: Authoritative Reference Framework · John C. Hull Chapter 8
steps: 1. Origin-to-Distribute Model: Banks sold mortgages to SPVs, severing credit risk and underwriting discipline.
2. Waterfall Subordination: Cash flows pay Senior first; credit defaults wipe out Equity first, then Mezzanine.
3. ABS CDO Engineering: Bundling BBB Mezzanine debt creates synthetic 75% AAA rated senior debt instruments.
4. Subprime Bubble Drivers: Teaser rates and NINJA loans enabled extreme leverage that collapsed upon rate resets.
5. Correlation Invariant: Geographic diversification collapsed when nationwide house price drops drove correlation to 1.
6. Bottom-Up Wipeout: A modest 10% collateral loss inflicts a 100% wipeout on Equity and 33.3% loss on Mezzanine.
7. Rating Agency Conflict: Issuer-pays incentives and benign historical samples systematically underpriced tail risk.
8. Basel III & Dodd-Frank: Post-crisis regulations enforced 7% CET1 buffers and 5% mandatory skin-in-the-game retention.
